signals.provenance_ref: ZATCA media release: Wave 25 integration-phase criteria (published 24 July 2026)
signals.buyer: CFO / finance operations / tax compliance lead
signals.problem: E-invoicing integration, VAT reporting accuracy, and reconciliation leakage as the integration threshold drops
signals.trigger: Wave 25 lowers the Phase-2 threshold to SAR 187,500 VAT-subject revenue in any of 2022-2025
facts: ZATCA set Wave 25 integration-phase criteria on 24 July 2026 for taxpayers whose VAT-subject revenue exceeded SAR 187,500 in 2022, 2023, 2024 or 2025.
Targeted taxpayers must integrate their e-invoicing solutions with the Fatoora platform by 1 February 2027.
Wave 25 is the first wave to include calendar-year 2025 revenue as a selection criterion and halves the prior threshold.
inferences: A materially larger population of smaller firms enters integration scope, plausibly raising demand for governed finance/tax automation help.
The deadline is a research trigger only; it does not prove that any specific firm wants external help or would buy.
unknowns: No named buyer has been confirmed as ZATCA-notified in Wave 25.
No purchase intent, budget, or incumbent-vendor evidence exists.
next_evidence: Confirm the Wave 25 notification timeline from ZATCA primary sources
Identify named firms in scope with public ERP/accounting transformation signals

The guidance being non-binding means procurement expectations, not statute, drive demand.

signals.provenance_ref: SDAIA enforcement record (48 decisions, Jan 2026) as reported by Clyde & Co, Latham & Watkins, Lexis Middle East
signals.authority_ref: SDAIA / PDPL Committees for Reviewing Violations
signals.problem: Consent management, marketing-consent proof, DPO appointment, 72-hour breach reporting and cross-border transfer safeguards
signals.trigger: SDAIA confirmed 48 PDPL enforcement decisions and penalties up to SAR 5,000,000 (doubled for repeat), including fines for marketing without explicit consent
facts: SDAIA confirmed 48 enforcement decisions in its January 2026 announcement; PDPL has been fully enforceable since 14 September 2024.
Penalty ceiling is SAR 5,000,000, doubling to SAR 10,000,000 for repeat violations; enforcement included marketing without explicit consent and 72-hour breach-notification failures.
Respondents have only five days to respond once notified of an alleged violation.
inferences: Enforcement maturity raises the value of demonstrable consent/breach/evidence operations, which is research-relevant to Dealix trust capabilities.
Recurring violation types are a proxy research agenda, not proof of demand from any named firm.
unknowns: SDAIA did not publish per-case penalty amounts or a numeric breakdown by category.
No named enforcement target is linked to a purchase signal.
next_evidence: Locate SDAIA primary enforcement notices with dates and categories
